title: Deploy: contrib/README.md setup guide
description:
Write contrib/README.md that explains how to deploy kithd using the systemd service files and musl static binary. This is the user-facing installation guide.

What: A markdown document that takes a new operator from zero to a running kithd instance.

Algorithm:
1. Create contrib/README.md with these sections:
   a. Prerequisites: Tailscale running (tailscaled), kithd binary obtained (download or build from source), Linux with systemd
   b. Installation steps (single user):
      - Copy kithd binary to /usr/local/bin/kithd
      - Copy contrib/systemd/kithd.service to /etc/systemd/system/
      - Create kithd system user: useradd --system --home /var/lib/kithd --shell /usr/sbin/nologin kithd
      - Create data directory: mkdir -p /var/lib/kithd && chown kithd:kithd /var/lib/kithd && chmod 700 /var/lib/kithd
      - Edit kithd.service: set KITHD_OWNER_ID to your Tailscale user ID (how to get it: tailscale status --json | jq .Self.UserID)
        NOTE: as of this version, KITHD_OWNER_ID can be omitted — kithd will auto-detect from Tailscale
      - systemctl daemon-reload && systemctl enable kithd && systemctl start kithd
      - systemctl status kithd (verify running)
   c. First-run experience: what the logs will say, what URL to open
   d. Multi-user template (org deployment): kithd@.service with %i substitution
   e. Musl binary info: what it is, how to verify (ldd), build from source commands
   f. Troubleshooting: Tailscale socket not found, port 443 permission issues, cert generation, journalctl commands
   g. Environment variable reference table (all KITHD_* vars, defaults, required/optional)

Defensive programming rules:
- Never document KITHD_BIND_ADDR as a production setting — it is development-only
- Include exact commands users should run; no hand-wavy instructions
- Include verification step after each major action
- Note that KITHD_OWNER_ID can be auto-detected but may be set explicitly as well
